first_impression.reaction: Two short paragraphs and then the script heading is right there. That's what I wanted. The intro tells me straight away the celebrant can 'read word for word', so I scrolled past the takeaways to the script. My only snag: the first takeaway is about Australian Marriage Act sections. I'm in Singapore and just wanted wording, so the first bullet felt like it was for someone else.

journey.quote: This sand ceremony script gives your celebrant something to read word for word: an introduction for your guests, the direction for the pour and the closing words.
journey.reaction: Good, it's telling me exactly what I'm getting. No fluff before the answer.

journey.quote: A sand ceremony is a symbolic ritual, so in Australia the legal words under sections 45 and 46 of the Marriage Act 1961 still have to be said around it.
journey.reaction: The first thing I read in the summary is legislation from a country I'm not marrying in. I wanted the wording. I'd have put the three-part bullet first, since that's actually what I searched for.

journey.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order.
journey.reaction: Reading fast on the train, 'well after' sounded like 'a long time after'. I had to read it twice to work out it means 'fits nicely after'. The FAQ answer has the same wording.

journey.section: Sand ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: Look at what you have made. Two colours, one vessel, and no way to tell where one of you ends and the other begins.
journey.reaction: Lovely, and I can copy it straight into a message to our celebrant. This is the bit I came for, and it's near the top.

journey.section: Sample sand ceremony wording for every kind of couple
journey.quote: Each version keeps the same three parts, so you can mix the introduction from one with the closing line of another.
journey.reaction: Handy. Clear headings for each tone mean I can jump straight to the short version or the romantic one without reading them all.

journey.quote: Copy this, fill in the blanks and send it to your celebrant.
journey.reaction: Bookmark-worthy. This is the bit I'd actually come back to.

journey.section: What you need for a sand ceremony
journey.quote: Sand in contrasting colours. Choose shades that read clearly side by side: ivory and sea blue, blush and charcoal.
journey.reaction: Useful list, but there's nothing on what a kit costs or where to get one. That's my next question.

journey.section: A sand ceremony and the legal words
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the form of ceremony sits in section 45 of the Marriage Act 1961
journey.reaction: Nice that it's dated, so I know it's current. But it's all Australian law and I skipped most of the section.

journey.quote: Your celebrant introduces the ritual, invites you to pour, then closes the moment with a line or two. The couple need say nothing at all.
journey.reaction: Short, direct FAQ answers. Exactly what I'd skim.

unanswered_questions: How much does a sand ceremony set (vessel, carafes, coloured sand) roughly cost, and where do people usually buy one?
How much sand do I need for two pourers versus a family pour?
Does any of the legal section apply if I'm not marrying in Australia (for example in Singapore)?

turn_offs_found.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome.
turn_offs_found.why: This is a direct answer to a question people search, but 'well after' reads like 'long after' on a quick skim, so the answer is fuzzier than it should be.

would_share_with: My fiancé, so we can pick a version

cta_reaction.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you as a single point of contact, working in your time zone.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a script, not a planner. It doesn't get in my way, which I appreciate, but I'm not at the stage of handing my wedding to anyone. I might tap the magazine link later if I'm bored on the train.
